_doc: Cases for the branch guard's git commit hook (#464, kind `commitHook`) and the branch-aware pre-commit gate (#613, kind `preCommitGate`), run against a real temporary git repository by both twins: adapters/js/hooks/__tests__/commit-hook-cases.test.mjs and adapters/python/hooks/test_commit_hook_cases.py. A third kind, `branchGuard` (#615), runs the PreToolUse branch guard in the repository, with `stdin` as its input. The kinds take the same fields: a `preCommitGate` row runs the gate where a `commitHook` row runs the wrapper, with its test command in `env.PLUMBLINE_TEST_CMD` (POSIX utilities only, so neither runner needs the other language); its `gateCopy` runs a copy of the gate instead, `alone`, or beside the guard and an empty commit hook (`emptyWrapper`) or the commit hook and an empty guard (`emptyGuard`), as an older release's files would lack what it reads; it cannot be combined with `commit`. CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR is cleared with the PLUMBLINE_* variables. Each row builds the repository in this order: `git init` on an unborn main; `committed` paths committed as the base, with `committedText` files (path to content) committed beside them (absent: main stays unborn); `side` paths committed on a branch named side, made from the base, then main checked out again; `branch` checked out as a new branch (null: HEAD detached at the base; "main": stay); `tags` created at HEAD; `headRef` given to `git symbolic-ref HEAD`; `config` pairs set with `git config`; `merge` arguments given to `git merge`; `rebaseStop` path committed on the current branch, then `git rebase --exec false HEAD~1` run so the rebase stops with HEAD detached and `rebase-merge/head-name` written, as at an `edit` stop; with `rebaseAlso`, that branch is pointed at the commit, a tip commit is added and `git rebase --update-refs --exec false HEAD~2` runs instead, so the rebase will move `rebaseAlso` too (`rebaseUpdateRefsDir` then replaces `update-refs` with a directory); with `rebaseApply`, `conflict.txt` is committed beside the path and `git rebase --apply` onto a branch that adds it differently stops on the conflict, writing `rebase-apply/head-name`; the rebase directory's `head-name` `rebaseHeadName` then deletes (null) or overwrites (text), or `rebaseHeadNameDir` replaces with a directory; `remove` and `move` applied with `git rm` and `git mv`; `stage` paths written and added; `stageHex` paths (hex bytes, which need not be UTF-8) added to the index only; `gitlink` paths added to the index as submodule commits (HEAD's); `stageCount` [prefix, n] adds n index-only paths prefix0 to prefix(n-1); `modify` paths rewritten without staging. Then the wrapper runs in the repository with `env` applied (null unsets) and every PLUMBLINE_* variable cleared first, or, when `commit` is present, a pre-commit hook that runs the wrapper is installed and `git commit` runs with those arguments, and a commit must be made exactly when `expectExit` is 0. `repo: false` runs the wrapper outside any repository instead. `fakeGit` ({script, executable}) runs the wrapper with PATH holding only a directory whose `git` is that script, made executable or not; it cannot be combined with `commit`. `expectStderr` is compared exactly.
